key_insight: Tabular foundation models can serve as highly competitive, out-of-the-box surrogates for Bayesian optimization in materials discovery.
engineering_relevance: These models could simplify materials-search workflows by reducing reliance on task-specific Gaussian process kernels and hyperparameter tuning.
method: Use TabPFN and TabICL as Bayesian optimization surrogate models.
Evaluate on two standard materials science benchmarks.
Compare against Gaussian processes, random forests, and CatBoost.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports highly competitive performance across two benchmarks without task-specific active-learning training or GP kernel selection.
watch_item: Results from two benchmarks do not establish reliability across broader materials domains or real laboratory campaigns.
paper_title: Out-of-the-Box Tabular Foundation Models for Bayesian Optimization in Materials Discovery
